title: Universal Beta Splatting
claim: Our method renders reflective and dynamic scenes close to ground truth, where the baseline loses detail or blurs.
layout: 2 scene groups; large GT/ours split image beside stacked baseline-vs-ours crops
description: The figure has two groups side by side, one for a static scene and one for a dynamic scene. Each group has a large image split diagonally by a white line. The left half is labeled GT (ground truth) and the right half is labeled Ours. Beside each large image are two stacked zoomed crops. In the static group, the crops are labeled 3DGS (top) and Ours (bottom). They show a kitchen counter with a bagged loaf of bread and a knife, and the glossy bag and metal pot look sharper in the Ours crop. In the dynamic group, the crops are labeled 4DGS (top) and Ours (bottom). They show a white volumetric cloud on a dark navy background. The 4DGS crop is blurry and smeared, and the Ours crop keeps crisp wispy detail. Small white label tags sit in the corners of each panel. The eye goes first to the large split images.
caption: Visualization of UBS rendering quality. For static real-world scenes (left), UBS achieves superior rendering of reflective and specular materials compared to 3DGS [ref]. For dynamic volumetric scenes (right), UBS maintains high visual fidelity in complex spatio-temporal scenarios where 4DGS [ref] produces blurring artifacts.
abstract: We introduce Universal Beta Splatting (UBS), a unified framework that generalizes 3D Gaussian Splatting to N-dimensional anisotropic Beta kernels for explicit radiance field rendering. Unlike fixed Gaussian primitives, Beta kernels enable controllable dependency modeling across spatial, angular, and temporal dimensions within a single representation. Our unified approach captures complex light transport effects, handles anisotropic view-dependent appearance, and models scene dynamics without requiring auxiliary networks or specific color encodings. UBS maintains backward compatibility by approximating to Gaussian Splatting as a special case, guaranteeing plug-in usability and lower performance bounds. The learned Beta parameters naturally decompose scene properties into interpretable without explicit supervision: spatial (surface vs. texture), angular (diffuse vs. specular), and temporal (static vs. dynamic). Our CUDA-accelerated implementation achieves real-time rendering while consistently outperforming existing methods across static, view-dependent, and dynamic benchmarks, establishing Beta kernels as a scalable universal primitive for radiance field rendering. Our project website is available at https://rongliu-leo.github.io/universal-beta-splatting/.
